hints: Find the parameter at $(e,3)$: $e^{\tan t}=e$ gives $\tan t=1$.
Differentiate both coordinates, using the chain rule in $dx/dt=e^{\tan t}\sec^2t$ and $dy/dt=6\tan t\sec^2t$.
Form $dy/dx=(dy/dt)/(dx/dt)$ and evaluate it when $\tan t=1$ to get the exact tangent gradient.
Use point-gradient form through $(e,3)$, then rearrange to $y=mx+c$.
walkthrough:
Determine the value of $\tan t$ at the point $(\mathrm{e}, 3)$:
$$x = \mathrm{e} \implies \mathrm{e}^{\tan t} = \mathrm{e}^1 \implies \tan t = 1$$
$$\text{Verify } y: \quad y = 3\tan^2 t = 3(1)^2 = 3 \quad (\text{consistent})$$
$$\text{Thus } \tan t = 1 \implies t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$$

Differentiate $x = \mathrm{e}^{\tan t}$ with respect to $t$ using the chain rule:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = \left(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}[\tan t]\right)\mathrm{e}^{\tan t} = \sec^2 t \cdot \mathrm{e}^{\tan t}$$

Differentiate $y = 3\tan^2 t$ with respect to $t$ using the chain rule:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = 3 \times 2\tan t \times \sec^2 t = 6\tan t\sec^2 t$$

Calculate the gradient $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ using the parametric rule:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y/\mathrm{d}t}{\mathrm{d}x/\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{6\tan t\sec^2 t}{\sec^2 t \cdot \mathrm{e}^{\tan t}} = \dfrac{6\tan t}{\mathrm{e}^{\tan t}} = 6\tan t \cdot \mathrm{e}^{-\tan t}$$

Substitute $\tan t = 1$ to find the numerical gradient $m$ of the tangent:
$$m = \dfrac{6(1)}{\mathrm{e}^1} = \dfrac{6}{\mathrm{e}}$$

Use the point-gradient line equation $y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)$ with $(x_1, y_1) = (\mathrm{e}, 3)$:
$$y - 3 = \dfrac{6}{\mathrm{e}}(x - \mathrm{e})$$
$$y - 3 = \dfrac{6}{\mathrm{e}}x - \left(\dfrac{6}{\mathrm{e}}\right)\mathrm{e}$$
$$y - 3 = \dfrac{6}{\mathrm{e}}x - 6$$
$$y = \dfrac{6}{\mathrm{e}}x - 6 + 3$$
$$y = \dfrac{6}{\mathrm{e}}x - 3$$
